title: GST 114 ( UNN ) : COMMON ERRORS IN SPEECH AND WRITING
subject: GST 114

questions.question: Errors in second language learning often arise from which cause?
options: Inability to internalize rules
Lack of exposure to media
Poor memory retention
Insufficient vocabulary
questions.explanation: Common errors occur due to the inability of learners to internalize grammar rules.

questions.question: Under which headings are common errors grouped?
options: Phonetic and lexical
Syntactic and semantic
Pragmatic and discourse
Morphological and syntactic
questions.explanation: Errors are grouped under headings such as syntactic, concord, semantic, and others.

questions.question: Which term refers to errors from misuse of parts of speech?
options: Semantic errors
Concord errors
Syntactic errors
Morphological errors
questions.explanation: Syntactic errors arise from the misuse of the parts of speech in sentences.

questions.question: The list of errors presented in the chapter is described as which of the following?
options: Exhaustive
Representative
Comprehensive
Definitive
questions.explanation: The list of errors is not exhaustive but representative of common mistakes.

questions.question: Errors arising from the misuse of word forms are classified as which type?
options: Syntactic
Semantic
Morphological
Concord
questions.explanation: Morphological errors refer to errors arising from the misuse of word forms.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a syntactic error?
options: I will discuss it during the next lecture
I will discuss about it during the next lecture
I will talk about it during the next lecture
I will mention it during the next lecture
questions.explanation: The verb discuss does not require the preposition about.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "I will discuss about it during the next lecture"?
options: I will discuss it during the next lecture
I will discuss on it during the next lecture
I will discuss for it during the next lecture
I will discuss at it during the next lecture
questions.explanation: The verb discuss takes a direct object without a preposition.

questions.question: Which sentence is syntactically correct?
options: The meeting has been fixed for next tomorrow
The meeting has been fixed for the day after tomorrow
The meeting has been fixed for tomorrow next
The meeting has been fixed for next tomorrow day
questions.explanation: The correct expression is the day after tomorrow, not next tomorrow.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "That boy plays truancy in the school"?
options: That boy plays truant in the school
That boy plays truancy at the school
That boy plays truant at the school
That boy plays truancy in school
questions.explanation: The correct idiom is to play truant, not to play truancy.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "You can pay me install mentally"?
options: You can pay me in installments
You can pay me install mentally
You can pay me with installments
You can pay me by installments
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is in installments, not install mentally.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "This laptop does not worth the price"?
options: This laptop is not worth the price
This laptop does not worthy the price
This laptop is not worthy the price
This laptop does not worth it the price
questions.explanation: The adjective worth is used with the verb is, not does.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "You are all welcomed"?
options: You are all welcome
You are all welcoming
You are all welcomed here
You are all welcomes
questions.explanation: The correct adjective is welcome, not welcomed.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "He is a coward man"?
options: He is a cowardly man
He is a coward man
He is a cowardice man
He is a cowards man
questions.explanation: The adjective form is cowardly, not coward.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a syntactic error?
options: She does not take anything seriously
He is a matured man
They are close friends
The news is good
questions.explanation: The correct adjective is mature, not matured.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "The girl is not taking her academic seriously"?
options: The girl is not taking her academics seriously
The girl is not taking her academic serious
The girl is not taking her academicals seriously
The girl is not taking her academic seriously
questions.explanation: The plural noun academics is used to refer to studies.

questions.question: Morphological errors refer to errors arising from which of the following?
options: Misuse of word forms
Misuse of sentence structures
Misuse of meanings
Misuse of punctuation
questions.explanation: Morphological errors arise from the misuse of word forms.

questions.question: Which word is not yet an English word?
options: Plump
Plumpy
Plumpness
Plumply
questions.explanation: Plumpy is not a standard English word; the correct word is plump.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "He is matured enough"?
options: He is mature enough
He is matured enough
He is maturing enough
He is maturity enough
questions.explanation: The adjective mature is used, not matured.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "You are adding much weight"?
options: You are putting on much weight
You are adding much weight
You are putting much weight
You are gaining much weight
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is putting on weight, not adding weight.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "The driver came back with a piece of good news"?
options: The driver came back with a piece of good news
The driver came back with a good news
The driver came back with good news
The driver came back with a piece of good news
questions.explanation: News is an uncountable noun, so a piece of news is correct.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "Going through the file, the error was discovered"?
options: Going through the file, I discovered the error
Going through the file, the error was discovered
Going through the file, the error discovered
Going through the file, the error was discovering
questions.explanation: The sentence has a dangling modifier; the subject must be the one performing the action.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "There are four alphabets in the word 'Alphabet'"?
options: There are four letters in the word 'Alphabet'
There are four alphabets in the word 'Alphabet'
There are four alphabet in the word 'Alphabet'
There are four alphabetic in the word 'Alphabet'
questions.explanation: The word alphabet refers to the whole set; individual units are letters.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "Hard work always results to success"?
options: Hard work always results in success
Hard work always results to success
Hard work always results for success
Hard work always results with success
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after result is in.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "The man is a staff of this University"?
options: The man is a member of staff of this University
The man is a staff of this University
The man is a staff in this University
The man is a staff at this University
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is a member of staff, not a staff.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "The lecture is not going to hold"?
options: The lecture is not going to take place
The lecture is not going to hold
The lecture is not going to holds
The lecture is not going to holding
questions.explanation: The correct expression is take place, not hold.

questions.question: Semantic errors result when wrong meanings are assigned to which of the following?
options: Words and structures
Sounds and letters
Punctuation marks
Sentence types
questions.explanation: Semantic errors result when wrong meanings are assigned to words and other syntactic structures.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "The two of us are close friends"?
options: Two of us are close friends
The two of us are close friends
The two of us is close friends
Two of us is close friends
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is two of us, not the two of us.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "Test and see that the Lord is good"?
options: Taste and see that the Lord is good
Test and see that the Lord is good
Taste and see that the Lord is good
Test and see that the Lord is good
questions.explanation: The correct idiom is taste and see, not test and see.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "There is no harm in trying"?
options: There is no harm in trying
There is no harm to try
There is no harm for trying
There is no harm to trying
questions.explanation: The correct expression is no harm in trying.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "Our tape recorder is damaged"?
options: Our tape recorder is spoilt
Our tape recorder is damaged
Our tape recorder is spoilt
Our tape recorder is damage
questions.explanation: The correct word for a machine that no longer works is spoilt.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "The man hears jargon"?
options: The man understands jargon
The man hears jargon
The man listens jargon
The man understands jargon
questions.explanation: The correct verb for understanding specialized language is understands.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "Uche arranged the hall orderly"?
options: Uche arranged the hall in an orderly manner
Uche arranged the hall orderly
Uche arranged the hall in orderly manner
Uche arranged the hall with orderly manner
questions.explanation: The adverb phrase is in an orderly manner.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "He bought a coloured television"?
options: He bought a colour television
He bought a coloured television
He bought a colouring television
He bought a colours television
questions.explanation: The correct adjective is colour, not coloured.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "He is matured enough to be responsible"?
options: He is mature enough to be responsible
He is matured enough to be responsible
He is maturing enough to be responsible
He is maturity enough to be responsible
questions.explanation: The adjective mature is used, not matured.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "You are adding much weight"?
options: You are putting on much weight
You are adding much weight
You are putting much weight
You are gaining much weight
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is putting on weight.

questions.question: Concord errors arise from lack of agreement in which area?
options: Number between subject and verb
Tense between clauses
Gender between pronouns
Case between nouns
questions.explanation: Concord errors arise from lack of agreement in number between subject and verb.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "The dupes has to be punished"?
options: The dupe has to be punished
The dupes has to be punished
The dupe have to be punished
The dupes have to be punished
questions.explanation: The singular form dupe is used with the singular verb has.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "He wants to credit Mathematics by all means"?
options: He wants to get credit in Mathematics by all means
He wants to credit Mathematics by all means
He wants to credit in Mathematics by all means
He wants to get credit for Mathematics by all means
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is get credit in a subject.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "My wife delivered her baby this morning"?
options: My wife gave birth to her baby this morning
My wife delivered her baby this morning
My wife delivered of her baby this morning
My wife gave birth her baby this morning
questions.explanation: The correct expression is gave birth to, not delivered.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "I will borrow you my book"?
options: I will lend you my book
I will borrow you my book
I will borrow you my book
I will lend you my book
questions.explanation: The correct verb is lend when giving something to someone.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "The film is titled Living in Bondage"?
options: The film is entitled Living in Bondage
The film is titled Living in Bondage
The film is title Living in Bondage
The film is entitled to Living in Bondage
questions.explanation: The correct word for a work's name is entitled.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "That bus will carry you to the town"?
options: That bus will take you to the town
That bus will carry you to the town
That bus will carry you to town
That bus will take you to town
questions.explanation: The correct verb for transporting people is take.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "The soup is sweet"?
options: The soup is tasty
The soup is sweet
The soup is sweeting
The soup is sweetened
questions.explanation: The correct word for pleasant taste is tasty or delicious.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "She doesn't know how to make soup"?
options: She doesn't know how to cook soup
She doesn't know how to make soup
She doesn't know how to prepare soup
She doesn't know how to making soup
questions.explanation: The correct verb for preparing soup is cook.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "You must leave your bad habits"?
options: You must give up your bad habits
You must leave your bad habits
You must give off your bad habits
You must leave off your bad habits
questions.explanation: The correct phrasal verb is give up.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "Please remind me of the story"?
options: Please remind me about the story
Please remind me of the story
Please remind me for the story
Please remind me on the story
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after remind is about.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "Our team defeated them by two goals to nothing"?
options: Our team defeated them by two goals to nil
Our team defeated them by two goals to nothing
Our team defeated them by two goals to zero
Our team defeated them by two goals to none
questions.explanation: The correct word for zero in sports is nil.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "If these shoes size you, buy them"?
options: If these shoes fit you, buy them
If these shoes size you, buy them
If these shoes suit you, buy them
If these shoes match you, buy them
questions.explanation: The correct verb for correct shoe size is fit.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "In spite of the new batteries, the radio refused to function"?
options: In spite of the new batteries, the radio refused to work
In spite of the new batteries, the radio refused to function
In spite of the new batteries, the radio refused to working
In spite of the new batteries, the radio refused to works
questions.explanation: The correct verb for a machine operating is work.

questions.question: What is the correct version of "NEPA has taken the light"?
options: NEPA has taken the power
NEPA has taken the light
NEPA has taken the electricity
NEPA has taken the current
questions.explanation: The correct term for electricity supply is power.
